changes: A watcher must itself be watched. Listings are read whole or not at all. Every new mechanism's proof names the event that proves it. Lessons go into reflections, so the next session inherits them. And a caution for the vision: 'click into place' is proven only when a project outside this circle adopts ocoeco on its own; until then the format must stay small, documented and robust, and that matters more than the user-facing part.
learned: Prove each mechanism by its own evidence, not by the path around it: I proved the watcher's alert, never its schedule. Prefer what says when it is cut short or stuck over what fails quietly. Look before editing: four failed edits came from guessing at code I had not read. The author's questions moved the design more than my plans did - each driver its own lease, the name oco-agent, tad's one concern, the shared GitHub budget. And on the author's larger point: open source has intelligence from the outside - CHAOSS has measured activity since 2017 - but not the inside: why things are so, what was decided and rejected, what is needed next and who is doing it. That inside is what ocoeco records, oco-agent coordinates and the observatory presents - the analysis half of BI and BA, which nobody had put in place.
over: 2026-11-11 evening to 2026-11-12 morning: tad's lost reasons restored and connected, SQL back in tad, oco-agent from its core to a service, the replays, and the watcher that never watched
saw: Every serious failure was silent. A listing that stopped at 1,000 without saying so made lab-agent run finished work again, twice. A request with no time limit most likely froze it. A schedule that never fired left the watcher blind for a night. A client stripped lines from inside a script. The shadow could not see jobs older than itself. And tad's reason to exist sat in a session log and an unmerged spike, so a rewrite dropped its SQL. Each time, what saved the work was a record that could be read cold, or a check that refused instead of passing.

changes: OCO and ocoeco will naturally expand into being a part of software: a user-facing part, robust and at one's fingertips, not depending on a web browser - a way for users to be connected to what they use: to see their apps' progress and the progress of the Linux phone they use, to see what needs focus and add their part, fill in the necessary pieces of information, make the necessary tests, provide feedback.
learned: ocoeco is the basic unit - a format, a protocol, a way of interacting with it, and of its interconnection: an ecosystem, for real.
over: Years of watching open source; the months since a research with Claude; what OCO and ocoeco have become
saw: Any big tech, any business has BI. Open source is not a business, and no one clicked into place that it lacks BI and BA - coordination, analysis, presentation. Now there is a working soul for it, OCO and ocoeco, which makes it possible with a simple and portable system, where ocoecos click into place with one another.
